courses.title: AI for data analysis
courses.description: Query databases, reports and dashboards with AI, with answers you can trace, to make better decisions in your operation and in transport.
courses.summary: Questions about databases, reports and dashboards, with an answer that can be checked.
courses.contact_body: Write what you want to be able to look up in your databases, reports or dashboards.

intro.text: Many operations already keep databases, reports, dashboards, sheets and indicators. The difficulty shows up when the question is not built into the dashboard, sources have to be crossed, or the answer needs context and not only a number.

lets you ask that question in ordinary language and query the source that fits. It does not replace the dashboards: it makes it easier to explore what already exists. The answer has to be checkable: which source it queried, which filters and dates it used, what calculation it made and what limits remain.

paragraphs.text: Start with the question, the sources and the judgment of the person who knows the operation. One answer opens the next: another period, another route, an exception or a summary.
In transport data, those questions can bring together routes, times, costs, events and compliance. In the operation, delays, capacity and incidents.

the AI working table

courses.title: AI for work teams
courses.description: Your team learns from cases in its own work, tries alternatives and leaves criteria and a path for keeping AI in use.
courses.summary: Cases from the team’s own work, alternatives they try, and a path to keep going.
courses.contact_body: Write the work the people who know each role want to explore.

intro.text: Bring together the people who know each role. They review the routine and decide what stays.

Applied AI learning follows that order: see where the effort, the sources and the decisions sit; try tools on a task the team knows; and write down what to use, what to correct and who is responsible for the next trial.
That is AI applied to the work.

courses.title: AI agents for real processes
courses.description: Define a task, connect sources, set limits and try an agent with human review, starting from a real process in your team.
courses.summary: A task, its sources, its limits and a trial with human review.
courses.contact_body: Write the work you want to describe, connect and try with human review.

intro.text: Creating AI agents starts by describing the work from beginning to end: the objective, the rules, who uses it and what delivery is expected. If that can be explained, it can already be tried. It is not about automating everything.
An agent works with a purpose, a context, sources, memory and rules. Besides the task, you agree how you will know it worked and what is recorded for the next step.

Agents in logistics and transport query authorised sources and the context of the operation. A person reviews the delivery.
